document.title: Leader Points Implementation & Production Migration Handoff
document.status: PRODUCTION MIGRATION UNDERWAY — GAME SYSTEM REV24, ADEPTA SORORITAS, AND ADEPTUS CUSTODES RUNTIME-VALIDATED
document.purpose: Continuity handoff for any AI resuming the 40k Reforged Leader Points migration. This document records the authoritative rules wording, the now-proven New Recruit architecture, the deliberate temporary dual-system migration strategy, completed production migrations, current canonical files, next steps, and the pitfalls/guardrails that must survive the rest of the rollout.
document.critical_instruction: Do not restart Leader Points research from first principles. The core LP cost/tracker/validation architecture has been prototype-tested and production-tested. Inspect the current canonical files listed below, preserve their stable IDs and dual-validator migration strategy, then continue catalogue-by-catalogue.
document.backup_and_recovery_policy: The user manages backups and manual rollback. Treat the current production path as a point of no return rather than creating extra safety branches/revisions solely for fear of rollback. If something catastrophic happens, the user will manually revert to a stable build.

executive_state.what_changed: Leader Capacity is being replaced by Leader Points as a weighted resource. Game Size grants 2 / 3 / 4 LP at 800 / 1200 / 1600 Points. Ordinary Leaders that previously counted toward Leader Maximum normally cost 1 LP. Special faction rules can charge more, including 'all of your Leader Points'.
executive_state.migration_state: The new weighted LP system and the old counted-Leader system intentionally run in parallel during catalogue migration. The old system remains live so unmigrated catalogues retain their previous legality. The new system becomes meaningful as each catalogue receives LP costs.
completed_production_migrations: Adeptus Custodes — complete and runtime-confirmed, including live 2 / 3 / 4 LP Game Size-dependent Shield-Captain costs.
executive_state.next_primary_target: Tyranids. Start from the current REV34 preview-updated catalogue, not REV33. Tyranids is the next useful stress test because the updated faction rule for Hive Tyrant uses the 'all of your Leader Points' pattern.

authoritative_rules.source: User-provided image of the updated Core Rules — SETUP > ARMY LIST BUILDING > ARMY LIST, supplied 2026-09-14.
authoritative_rules.source_policy: Rules text shown to players must use official source phrasing. Listbuilder error messages may be custom-written for clarity and repair guidance. Do not editorialize source-derived faction rule descriptions merely to update terminology.
authoritative_rules.general_army_list_text_verbatim: The size of players’ army lists are measured in points. Choose a size for the battle from below. Each player can select units for their army list totalling up to that size. Each size comes with list building restrictions and a number of leader points to spend on adding leader units to your army. You must spend one leader point to add a leader unit to your army list.

faction_overrides.principle: Faction-specific source rules may override the ordinary one-Leader-point cost. Do not force all tagged Leaders to 1 LP when the authoritative faction PDF says otherwise.
faction_overrides.known_pattern: Shield-Captain and Hive Tyrant source rules use the concept '<all of your Leader Points>'. The user explicitly wants this represented as 2 LP at 800, 3 LP at 1200, and 4 LP at 1600. Hardcoding those values by Game Size is accepted and preferred over unnecessary abstraction if it is simpler and robust.

leader_points_tracker.display_semantics: Leader Points (remaining/max), where the first number is remaining LP, not spent LP.
leader_points_tracker.overspend_display: Clamp remaining display to 0/max; never show negative Leader Points.
leader_points_tracker.missing_entry_protection: Army > Configuration has a constructive error if Leader Points is deleted: 'Leader Points is missing. The listbuilder needs this entry to track your remaining Leader Points and validate Leader Point spending. Add Leader Points back under Configuration.'
leader_points_tracker.duplicate_protection: The tracker remains an automatically managed permanent Configuration entry.

legacy_system_during_migration.mechanism: Count selections carrying Counts Toward Leader Maximum.
legacy_system_during_migration.reason: Preserves old legality for unmigrated catalogues and provides an independent live checksum while migrated catalogues gain weighted LP costs.
legacy_system_during_migration.expected_temporary_behavior: A migrated illegal roster may trigger both the old count error and the new LP error. This is acceptable during migration. The legacy validator is weaker than LP for a variable-cost Leader but does not contradict it.

intentional_non_features: No native LP roster cost limit. LP defaultCostLimit remains -1.
No explicit 0 LP resource entries or costs.
Game Size no longer owns the new weighted LP error; Leader Points owns it.
Rare, attachments, pooled faction limits, Additional Copy Costs, ratios, subfactions, and other legality systems are independent and untouched.

proven: Positive LP costs display natively on units and in roster totals.
Roster-scope conditions can query the summed LP cost type directly.
LP total can drive the live remaining/max tracker name.
A 3-LP Leader plus a 1-LP Leader fails at a 3-LP budget even though only two Leaders are selected.
Changing Game Size updates the LP budget/tracker.
Nested/shared/imported Leader costs can aggregate exactly once without double-charging.
Explicit 0 LP is suppressed by New Recruit's native visible cost display.
Ordinary 1-LP production Leaders work under GS24.
The old counted-Leader validator and new LP system coexist.
Nested Imagifier remains uncharged when it has no LP cost.
Existing faction mechanics survive the migration.
A production unit LP cost can change live with Game Size.
Hardcoded 2 / 3 / 4 LP modifiers are a valid implementation of 'all your Leader Points'.
Rare and a stronger independent SHIELD-CAPTAIN max-1 restriction coexist with LP without interference.
The legacy Counts Toward Leader Maximum tag can remain active alongside a variable weighted LP cost.

not_separately_runtime_proven_after_late: The final placement of weighted LP overspend errors on the Leader Points tracker rather than Game Size has been implemented and structurally validated, but the conversation does not contain an explicit targeted runtime test of that exact moved-error UI.

The parent-level 'Leader Points is missing' deletion-recovery error has been implemented and structurally validated, but the conversation does not contain an explicit targeted runtime test where the user deletes the tracker.

ordinary_positive_lp_leader.rule: During migration, Counts Toward Leader Maximum is the roadmap for which existing selections participate in the LP economy. If the source has no special LP rule, give the tagged selection 1 LP.

no_lp_spend.rule: There is no production concept of '0 LP'. If a Leader spends no Leader Points, do not add an LP cost at all. Do not add explicit zero-valued LP costs for consistency.

all_leader_points_pattern.implementation: Give the unit an LP cost with base value 2, then set the LP cost field to 2 / 3 / 4 under roster conditions for 800 / 1200 / 1600 Game Size. Hardcoding the three values is explicitly approved by the user.
all_leader_points_pattern.important: This is an intrinsic unit LP cost, not a second hidden counting system. The LP cost remains the weighted arithmetic authority.

preserved: Counts Toward Leader Maximum on the four historically counted Leaders.
Counts Toward Leader Maximum on all three.

core_principles: Use the legacy Counts Toward Leader Maximum category as the migration roadmap/checksum. Do not write a separate Leader inventory report unless a real ambiguity requires one.
Do not infer LP spending from the visible Leader category.
Do not encode 0 LP. A selection either has a positive LP cost or it does not.
Preserve the old hidden category and old Game Size count validator until every catalogue is converted.
LP is the new weighted arithmetic authority. The old count system remains only as temporary compatibility enforcement/checksum.
Rules text must come from authoritative PDFs/source images; error messages may be custom.
Preserve stable IDs for all existing semantic objects.
Do not redesign unrelated functioning mechanics during LP migration.
Runtime-test the tricky faction-specific behavior after implementation rather than repeatedly re-proving basic LP arithmetic.
migration_policy.release_and_commit_policy: Incremental production commits are acceptable. The user is not concerned about mixed-version deployment and manages backups manually. Because the legacy validator remains active, unmigrated catalogues preserve their old legality, although their LP tracker will not yet reflect Leader expenditure until migrated.

catalogue_migration_workflow.details: Do not accidentally migrate an older snapshot. Check for any newer maintenance work first.

catalogue_migration_workflow.action: Leave untagged/exempt Leaders without an LP cost.
Put LP on the semantic owner exactly once.
catalogue_migration_workflow.details: Native unit owns native LP. Complete reusable shared root normally owns intrinsic LP. Consumer entryLinks must not duplicate an intrinsic shared-root LP cost. If a consumer-specific exception ever exists, model that exception locally rather than corrupting the reusable root.
Rare, attachment legality, pooled faction caps, copy costs, ratios, subfaction gates, and other semantics are not replaced by LP.

catalogue_migration_workflow.action: Increment catalogue revision and update durable comments.
catalogue_migration_workflow.details: Record the LP migration and GS24 retarget. Do not rewrite source-derived faction rules without updated authoritative wording.
Valid JSON; zero duplicate IDs; pre-existing IDs preserved; old leader tags preserved; only intended LP costs/modifiers added; existing Points and unrelated mechanics unchanged.
Examples: nested counted Leader, Countless/nested exempt Leader, imported/shared Leader, 'all LP' Leader, or any faction-specific pooled restriction.

catalogue_migration_workflow.action: Move on after the targeted test passes.
catalogue_migration_workflow.details: No need to produce a separate migration report or re-audit the whole project after every file.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: LP on both a shared root and its consumer entryLink would spend the resource twice.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Put intrinsic LP on the semantic owner once. Runtime-test shared paths when first encountered in production.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.risk: Missing charges on structurally unusual Leaders
pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Compiled variants, non-attaching Leaders, nested counted Leaders, and imported roots may not look like ordinary Leaders.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Use Counts Toward Leader Maximum as the migration roadmap, not names or visible Leader category membership.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.risk: Treating every tagged Leader as exactly 1 LP
pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Source rules can define weighted costs such as all available Leader Points.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: The old tag means 'participates in the LP economy', not 'cost is always 1'. Check authoritative faction rules for exceptions.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Rare, pooled caps, attachments, ratios and copy costs answer different legality questions.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: LP is additive. Never remove or collapse unrelated restrictions because LP now exists.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.risk: Rare being accidentally treated as a Leader Point mechanic
pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Rare is a unique independent category and must survive exactly.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Preserve Rare semantics/validation untouched unless the authoritative faction rules separately change them.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.risk: Cost modifiers touching the wrong cost type
pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Existing Points modifiers must not accidentally mutate LP, and LP Game Size modifiers must target the LP cost type ID.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Inspect cost modifiers on migrated Leaders; target Points and LP explicitly by their canonical cost IDs.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Players must never see negative remaining LP or stale max values.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Use complete 800/1200/1600 tracker states; overspend clamps to 0/max; Game Size switching must update immediately.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.risk: Deleting the Leader Points tracker disables validation silently
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: REV24 has a parent-level constructive missing-entry error. Preserve it.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Some faction PDFs may still contain old Leader Capacity wording until their authoritative source changes.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Use official rules wording verbatim where source-derived. Update internal comments freely; custom builder errors may use current LP terminology.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Combining LP work with unrelated refactors increases regression risk.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Make LP migration mechanically narrow. Strange-but-working structures are not defects.

pitfalls_and_guardrails.risk: Selected-hidden or fragile New Recruit patterns
pitfalls_and_guardrails.why_it_matters: Known engine hazards remain hazards during LP work.
pitfalls_and_guardrails.guardrail: Do not introduce selected-hidden flows; runtime-test unfamiliar engine-sensitive structures.

cleanup_after_full_migration.timing: ONLY after every active catalogue and relevant shared library has been converted and verified.
planned_actions: Remove the old count-based Leader Capacity validators from Game Size.
Run representative smoke tests: ordinary standalone, nested Leader, shared/imported Leader, and all-LP Leader.
Search player-facing listbuilder-owned wording for stale Leader Capacity / Leader slot terminology.
Review Counts Toward Leader Maximum as a separate cleanup decision: keep, rename while preserving ID, or remove if genuinely redundant.
Do not automatically delete the old hidden category merely because the count validator is removed.
cleanup_after_full_migration.not_required: Do not perform a giant faction-by-faction re-audit after the migration. The user prefers targeted runtime checks during conversion plus representative smoke tests at the end.

superseded_or_historical_files.note: These remain useful for archaeology but are not current production baselines. The canonical REV24 file includes dual validation, weighted errors on the Leader Points tracker, and missing-tracker protection.

alternative_architectures_considered.name: Rename existing hidden count category and continue counting Leaders
alternative_architectures_considered.reason: It preserves today's 1-LP equivalence but cannot naturally express Hive Tyrant = 3 LP. It would be a Leader Capacity system wearing Leader Points vocabulary.

alternative_architectures_considered.name: Duplicate hidden category/count objects to simulate weight
alternative_architectures_considered.reason: Brittle, implementation-heavy, poor semantic correspondence, and likely to create special cases for every non-1 LP Leader.

alternative_architectures_considered.name: Game Size adds positive LP and Leaders subtract negative LP
alternative_architectures_considered.reason: It makes the roster total equal remaining LP, which is attractive for the counter, but native unit costs would become negative ('-1 LP' for a Leader), which communicates the opposite of 'this unit costs 1 LP'.

alternative_architectures_considered.name: ACC-style separate Configuration ledger only
alternative_architectures_considered.reason: Could calculate resource use, but duplicates arithmetic across catalogues and makes future variable LP costs more cumbersome. Use only if New Recruit cannot query/custom-validate a custom LP cost cleanly.

confidence_legend.DIRECT_EVIDENCE: The cited source directly demonstrates the behavior.
confidence_legend.STRONG_INFERENCE: The source demonstrates adjacent/general schema capability; exact Reforged/NR behavior still needs a test.
confidence_legend.HYPOTHESIS: Plausible implementation idea not yet directly demonstrated.

findings.finding: BattleScribe/New Recruit data supports multiple independent cost types.
evidence: BSData Battlegroup.gst defines pts, BR, Men, Officers, and Scouts cost types.
Warhammer 40,000 9th edition data defines pts, PL, and CP cost types.

findings.finding: A selectable entry can carry a non-points custom cost and New Recruit exposes it.
evidence: New Recruit Wiki Command Points entry: Costs: 1 CP.
New Recruit Wiki Shared Faction Bonus: Costs: 2 CP, with modifier changing it to 3 CP.

findings.finding: Custom cost values can be modified conditionally.
evidence: New Recruit Wiki Shared Faction Bonus shows 'set CP 3' under a roster condition.
8th-edition Marneus Calgar Wiki entries show 'set CP 2' when Warlord is selected.

findings.finding: Roster cost objects have both value and optional limit in BattleScribe-compatible tooling.
evidence: BSData Project Phalanx documents IRosterCostSymbol as having both value and limit.

findings.finding: Other BattleScribe systems use multiple custom resource-like costs on units.
evidence: Battlegroup unit/library data contains nonzero BR, Men, Officers, and Scouts costs on selections.

findings.finding: A custom LP total should be usable as the weighted resource authority.
evidence: Custom cost types aggregate on roster entries in BattleScribe-compatible data.
Cost values are modifiable and roster costs have values/limits.
Exact condition-query syntax/behavior for an arbitrary LP cost total in current New Recruit is not yet proven in Reforged.

findings.finding: A dynamic tracker name driven directly by LP total is likely possible.
evidence: Reforged already uses name modifiers elsewhere and BattleScribe conditions can query roster data.
The exact combination 'custom cost total -> name modifier' still requires runtime proof.

historical_prototype_matrix_updated.question: Does New Recruit visibly show a custom LP cost on a selected/unit entry?
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.result: Positive LP costs display natively; no name hacks required.

historical_prototype_matrix_updated.question: How does New Recruit display 0 LP?
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.result: Native 0 LP is visually suppressed. User decision: do not encode 0 LP at all; absence of LP cost means no spend.

historical_prototype_matrix_updated.question: Can a roster-scope condition query total custom LP cost?
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.result: Yes; this is the production weighted arithmetic authority.

historical_prototype_matrix_updated.question: Can LP total drive the tracker name?
Can custom LP error validation trigger from weighted LP total rather than Leader count?
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.result: Yes; 3-LP + 1-LP overspend was proven in the disposable test system.

historical_prototype_matrix_updated.question: Should Game Size set a native LP roster cost limit?
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.result: LP defaultCostLimit remains -1. Custom tracker/errors provide the required UX and wording.

historical_prototype_matrix_updated.question: Does changing Game Size update tracker/max and LP costs?
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.result: Budget changes were proven in prototype; Custodes production additionally proves unit LP itself can change 2 / 3 / 4 by Game Size.

historical_prototype_matrix_updated.question: Do nested/shared/consumer-linked Leaders preserve LP cost exactly once?
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.status: PASS IN DISPOSABLE TEST; CONTINUE TARGETED PRODUCTION CHECKS
historical_prototype_matrix_updated.result: Prototype confirmed exact-once aggregation. Continue checking real shared dependency clusters when reached.

do_not_do: Do not revert to Leader-count arithmetic as the final Leader Points implementation.
Do not delete or rename Counts Toward Leader Maximum during the migration.
Do not turn off the legacy Game Size count validator until all catalogue migrations are complete.
Do not infer LP cost from visible Leader category membership.
Do not give every tagged Leader 1 LP without checking for an authoritative weighted-cost exception.
Do not add explicit 0 LP costs. No LP cost means no LP spend.
Do not duplicate an intrinsic shared-root LP cost on consumer entryLinks.
Do not make unspent Leader Points illegal.
Do not introduce a native LP cost limit without a new deliberate decision.
Do not remove Rare, attachment, pooled faction, ratio, copy-cost, or other independent restrictions as part of LP migration.
Do not rewrite source-derived rule text merely to harmonize terminology.
Do not resume from superseded REV24 Game System candidate files.
Do not restart the prototype/research phase unless current production behavior actually contradicts the proven architecture.
Do not create a giant final audit/report unless the user explicitly asks for one.
